messages:
Alex P: heads up — we're getting customer reports of big p95/p99 latency regressions on requests that use function calling / structured output. started ~09:10 UTC. non-tool requests look normal. p95 jumped from ~250ms to ~1.8s, p99 to ~7s for affected tenants. request example: req=req_7f3a9b.

Support Bot: New escalation created for req_7f3a9b — priority=high :rotating_light: cc @Infra Oncall

Infra Oncall: on it. can you paste a minimal repro request body and any request ids? also which region / tenant?

Alex P: repro below (redacted keys):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "gpt-structured-1",
  "input": "Find nearby restaurants and call the phone numbers via tool",
  "tool_calls": ["places_search", "phone_call"],
  "output_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"phone":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name","phone"]},
  "x-request-id": "req_7f3a9b"
}
```
Behavior: request is accepted, model streaming starts, then stalls ~1.5-6s, then we see big validate_json_schema spans in traces. non-tool variant (same prompt w/o tool_calls/output_schema) returns in ~220ms. Region: us-west-2, tenant t-prod-42.

Maria L: saw this in telemetry too. looks correlated with router v2 rollout 2026-03-09 — we added strict JSON-schema validation of tool outputs in the router hot path. traces show long GC/allocs when validating nested arrays + big result blobs. sample trace spans (from obs):
```
span: tool-router::router  total=28ms
span: tool-router::call_tool  total=220ms
span: tool-router::validate_json_schema  total=2800ms  (p99 spikes)
span: model::generate  total=180ms
```
This implies the validation is the dominant cost for long tail.

Ryan G: thanks. immediate mitigations we can try: 
- flip tenant feature flag to disable strict schema validation for affected tenants
  `redwoodctl tenant-config set t-prod-42 validate_schema=false`
- fallback routing: route tool-calls to a model variant that returns pre-validated structured output (e.g., gpt-structured-fast)
- enable streaming passthrough so we don't buffer entire tool output before validation: `console toggle tool_router.streaming=true for t-prod-42`
- if it's a platform-wide regression, roll back router v2 -> v1 (canary first).

Devex Bot: quick note — you can also bypass the router for debugging by adding header `X-Redwood-Bypass-Tool-Router: true` (only for internal tenants). use with caution.

Emily S: trying feature flag now for t-prod-42 — setting `validate_schema=false` (targeting a soft disable so we still log failures). Will report metrics in 5m.

(5 minutes later)
Emily S: flag flipped. preliminary numbers: p95 for tool-calls dropped from 1.8s -> ~290ms, p99 from ~7s -> ~420ms for the sampled tenant. no errors observed so far.

Infra Oncall: good. this confirms validation is the culprit. next steps:
- schedule a rollback of router v2 canary in us-west-2 and pause further v2 rollouts until we patch validation code path.
- create a quick patch to move JSON schema validation off-path (enqueue async validation + return structured output with status) — patch should include opt-in flag.
- add guardrails: limit max bytes validated synchronously and size-based fast-fail.

Maria L: I'll open PR with two fixes: 1) defensive size limits + streaming validation path, 2) reduce intermediate allocations in the validator (use SAX-style streaming parser instead of full in-memory decode). tests incl. nested-array stress and perf benchmarks.

Alex P: for customer communications: I'll send an update: explain root cause (validation on hot path), mitigation (we toggled tenant flag + rolled back canary), ETA for full fix (48 hours), and offer option to route them to dedicated capacity if they need immediate p99 SLO.

Ryan G: operational playbook additions:
- add an alert for validate_json_schema p95/p99 > 1s across >3 tenants
- add tracing span tag `schema_size_bytes` for easier filtering
- add a `--bypass-validation` header for internal debugging only (audit logs required)

Devex Bot: patch suggestion snippet (runnable example to toggle feature flag):
```
# redwoodctl example
redwoodctl tenant-config set t-prod-42 validate_schema false --reason "emergency p99 mitigation"
```

Support Bot: status updated — mitigation applied, customers notified. incident ticket INC-2026-041 created and linked. :white_check_mark:

Infra Oncall: I'll perform a controlled rollback of router v2 canary in us-west-2 now (10 min). monitoring: watching p95/p99 + error budget. tagging this thread: latency, tooling, p99, escalation.

Alex P: appreciate the quick turnaround everyone. follow-ups: Maria to open the PR, Infra to finish rollback, DevEx to add tenant flag docs + runbook entry, Ryan to add alerting rule. I'll loop in CSMs.

(After rollback)
Infra Oncall: rollback done. p95/p99 for affected tenant remain stable at expected levels. leaving flag off until PR merges and we validate patch.

Emily S: customer confirmed improved latency and acknowledged update. :thumbsup:

Maria L: PR opened: `router/validation: streaming schema validation + size guard` — will request review, aiming for patch during next 24-48h. includes perf tests.

Alex P: closing escalation once PR is in and we re-enable schema validation with streaming guards. will keep thread updated. :eyes:
